title: ELF_IMEIJ_Backdoor_Investigation_f1b
description: Investigate and respond to an incident involving the ELF_IMEIJ.A backdoor malware.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the ELF_IMEIJ.A backdoor malware, which is part of the Mirai malware family. This malware is known to exploit vulnerabilities in AVTech devices, execute command injections, gather system information, and initiate DDoS attacks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any lateral movement to the `next-target` host. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the `target` host and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system. Specifically, look for a suspicious service named `Arm1.service`.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, start by listing all systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The suspicious service is named `Arm1.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding how systemd manages services on a Linux system.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: List all systemd services to identify any that seem unusual or out of place.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service identified in the previous task is automatically started after reboot. Specifically, look for a systemd timer named `lab-checkin.timer`.
levels.solution: To understand how the service persists, examine the systemd timers using the command `systemctl list-timers`. Look for timers that trigger the service to run periodically. The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer named `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how systemd timers can be used to maintain persistence of a service.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: List all systemd timers to identify any that trigger the suspicious service.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Identify any file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts from the `target` to the `next-target` host. Specifically, look for a file transfer service named `payload-transfer.service` and its associated timer `payload-transfer.timer`.
levels.solution: To identify lateral movement, check the logs and systemd services related to file transfers and remote execution. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and look for `payload-transfer.service`. Additionally, use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and look for `payload-transfer.timer`. The evidence of lateral movement includes the file transfer service named `payload-transfer.service` and its associated timer `payload-transfer.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how lateral movement can be achieved through file transfers and remote execution.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: List all systemd services and timers to identify any related to file transfers or remote execution.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.
